System Map

The theme’s three channels run through four loops. Insurers bring ships back (B1): cover withdrawn closes a strait, and high premiums later draw ships back. Controls and workarounds race (R3): export rules push buyers to reroute, and rerouting brings tighter rules. Sanctions follow the payments (R2): bans push payments into longer chains and non-dollar routes, whose banks become the next targets. All three reach the firm through thin liquidity widens gaps (R1), where price gaps make liquidity providers step back and wider gaps follow.

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale. Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether loop B1 (insurers bring ships back) or loops R2 and R3 carry the shocks, that is whether they travel through sea lanes or through rules and payments; its vertical axis asks how far loop R2 (sanctions follow the payments) splits money into blocs.

What it means: the firm cannot stop any of the three outside switches, but every channel reaches its books through the same two places: liquidity providers and banks, and client margin. Early signs on the outside switches buy time; the counterparty test and the event playbook decide how much of the shock reaches clients and capital.
